title: Building your circle
hook: You don't need a crowd. You need one mentor, one friend and one class.

screens.text: The shahada can come with hugs and smiles, and then a quiet week. If it's felt lonely, you're not imagining it, and it doesn't mean you chose wrong. Today you start building your circle on purpose.
**You weren't meant to do this alone.** In a large survey of American converts, loneliness was one of the hardest parts, especially around holidays [Yaqeen 2025].
bubbles: Faith grows faster with people around you.

screens.before: In that survey, the converts who did best had
screens.after: at the masjid and a real connection there.

options.feedback: Yes. Friends at the masjid made the biggest difference [Yaqeen 2025].
Not quite. It was friends at the masjid and a real connection there [Yaqeen 2025].
Not quite. Books help, but people made the difference: friends at the masjid [Yaqeen 2025].

screens.text: **Company shapes you.** The Prophet ﷺ compared a good friend to someone who sells perfume: even if you buy nothing, you leave smelling good [Bukhari 2101].
bubbles: He also taught that people tend to take on the ways of their close friends, so choose them with care [Abu Dawud 4833].
Keep your old friends too, with kindness [Q 60:8]. Step back only from what pulls you away from Allah [Field Guide ch. 12].

screens.prompt: Your old friends: keep it, or step back?

items.text: Coffee with a college friend who isn't Muslim
items.why: Keep it. Islam asks you to be kind to friends who aren't Muslim [Q 60:8].

items.text: A nights-out routine built around drinking
items.why: Step back from the drinking, not the person. Suggest a meal or a game instead.

items.text: Pickup basketball with your usual crew
items.why: Keep it. Nothing here pulls you away from Allah.
Keep it. Eat what's halal for you, and enjoy the company.

screens.title: Your circle: three people to find

cards.back: Someone further along who you can text with questions: {{mentor.name}}, or someone your imam suggests. Not someone you met online last week.
A Muslim around your age and stage of life, ideally another convert. Someone you'd grab food with, not just pray next to.
A weekly halaqa (study circle), a new-Muslim class or a youth night at {{masjid.name}}. Showing up weekly matters more than which class.

screens.situation: After Jumu'ah, a woman invites Hannah to a new-Muslim dinner on Saturday. Hannah's tired, a bit shy, and doesn't know anyone going.

options.text: Say yes, and ask if she can come with someone
options.feedback: Great choice. Arriving with someone makes it easier. One dinner can turn into a real friend.
Very human. But these invites don't always come twice. Going once, even for an hour, is worth it.

options.text: Decline. She'll wait until she knows more
options.feedback: Not quite. You don't need to know more to belong. People there were new once too.

screens.text: **A word of care.** Real friends and mentors never rush you. If someone does, step back and tell {{mentor.name}}.
bubbles: {teen}Under 18? Your mentor will be an adult the masjid has checked, messages include a second adult, and meetings happen in public masjid spaces.{/teen}

screens.prompt: A good friend, or a warning sign?

items.text: Invites you to a class at the masjid, no pressure
items.why: Healthy. An open invite you can take or leave.

items.text: Pushes you to get married quickly
items.why: Warning sign. Real friends never rush you. Tell your mentor.
Warning sign. Be cautious, and talk to your mentor.

items.text: Wants you to join their group and drop everyone else
items.why: Warning sign. Pulling you toward a new group, away from others, is a red flag.

items.text: Says to cut off your family
items.why: Warning sign. Islam asks you to be good to your family. Tell your mentor.

items.text: Lets you go at your own pace
items.why: Healthy. Good company never rushes you.

screens.prompt: Draw your circle. Who do you already have (a mentor, a Muslim friend, a class)? Which one is missing, and what's one step toward it this week?

chips: Where can I find other converts near me?
I feel awkward at the masjid. Any tips?
How do I keep my non-Muslim friends?

steps: Send {{mentor.name}} a short note on how your week's going
Add one question you have. Two lines counts
screens.optional_extra: Ask {{masjid.name}} or your mentor which class or social night is coming up, and put it in your calendar.

screens.text: One mentor, one friend, one class. Good company makes faith easier, and kindness keeps your old friendships too.
Circles are built one message and one dinner at a time.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Loneliness after the shahada is the most common convert struggle; friends at the masjid and mosque attachment predict better outcomes; about 40% feel lonely at Ramadan or Eid [Yaqeen 2025 (Becoming Muslim); Research Notes - Retention and Convert Voices].
- Good company: the perfume seller and the blacksmith [Bukhari 2101]; people take on their close friends' ways [Abu Dawud 4833, hasan per al-Albani]; keep company that helps you [Revealed Path ch. 17].
- Keep non-Muslim friends with kindness [Q 60:8]; step back only from what pulls you away from your faith [Field Guide ch. 12].
- Warning signs: pressure toward quick marriage, money, a group, or isolation from family; route to the mentor (Spec §6.2 rule 12).
- For under-18s: safeguarding rules (vetted same-gender mentor where possible, no private one-to-one messages, public masjid spaces).
- Today al-Ikhlas is complete; the convert now recites al-Fatiha then al-Ikhlas in the first two rak'ahs of each prayer, al-Fatiha alone in rak'ahs 3–4 [First Instructions on Worship ch. 7].

**Likely questions**
- *"Where do I find other converts?"* Ask the masjid about a new-Muslim class or convert circle; ask the mentor for introductions. Don't name specific online groups.
- *"I feel awkward at the masjid."* Normal. Go at the same time each week, arrive a little early, stay a few minutes after, and say salam to one person.
- *"My old friends drink and party."* Keep the friendship where you can (coffee, sports, a meal); skip what's haram; be honest and kind. Day 13 and Day 56 cover more.
- *"No one replies to me at the masjid / my mentor is slow."* Validate; suggest one more try, then use "Ask my imam" to ask the masjid for a mentor. Never blame the convert.
- *"Can I meet my mentor alone?"* For adults: public places at the masjid are best at first. For under-18s: never one-to-one; a second adult is always included.

**Escalate:** someone pressuring the convert toward marriage, money or isolation; any sign of grooming or exploitation (especially with minors); a convert with no mentor assigned (send to the masjid queue). Danger at home follows the safety rule.

**Don't**
- Don't tell them to drop non-Muslim friends.
- Don't push marriage as the cure for loneliness, especially for teens.
- Don't shame them for not having a circle yet.
